Scenario: You finally get your driver’s license and ask your dad to borrow the family car to drive to the movies. As your dad hands you the keys, he looks tense and nervous. As you walk to the car, you think that his reaction to you driving alone for the first time is untrusting.
Comprehension Question: Does your dad's nervous reaction make you assume he doesn't trust you to drive alone?

Scenario: Someone in your grade posts a picture of the car their parents got them for their 16th birthday. Your family shares a single car, and your parents would not be able to afford to buy another one. You think about the gifts your parents have given you over the years, and you feel let down.
Comprehension Question: Are you feeling appreciative of your parents' past gifts when you see your classmate's new car?

Scenario: Your friend is celebrating their anniversary with their significant other and texts you a cute picture. Seeing the picture makes you think about how you've never been in a real relationship before. You imagine yourself celebrating an anniversary with your own significant other one day, and you feel dejected.
Comprehension Question: Does seeing your friend's anniversary photo leave you feeling dejected about your own relationship status?

Scenario: You’re the only one in your friend group who hasn’t had your first kiss. When your friends talk about their experiecnes, you feel embarassed and left out. You remind yourself that real connection matters more than timing, and you feel sorry for yourself.
Comprehension Question: Even after reminding yourself that connection matters more than timing, do you still feel sorry for yourself?

Scenario: Your friend is giving a presentation in English class and she seems totally confident and calm. You think about how when you give presentations, your hands shake and your stomach twists with nerves. You feel frustrated that public speaking doesn't come as naturally to you.
Comprehension Question: Are you at ease with public speaking the way your friend seems to be?

Scenario: At lunch, your friends are talking about their dates for the school dance and what they are planning to wear. You feel sad that you don't have a date to the dance yet. If you go to the dance without a date, you will have a bad time no matter what.
Comprehension Question: Will going to the dance without a date guarantee that you have a bad time?

Scenario: You start your first part-time job and make a small mistake on your first shift. Your manager sighs and looks annoyed but tells you that it's okay. They probably think you are incompotent.
Comprehension Question: After your manager sighs, do you assume they think you're incompetent?

Scenario: Most of your friends already have a job lined up for summer vacation. It's almost the end of the school year and you haven't even started applying. You think about the different types of jobs you could apply for, and you feel anxious.
Comprehension Question: Are you feeling calm about not having applied for a summer job yet?

Scenario: You scroll through your feed and see a friend’s post showing their academic achievements. You think about how your grades aren't as good, and start feeling like you're not measuring up. It leaves you feeling disappointed.
Comprehension Question: Does comparing your grades to your friend's achievements leave you feeling disappointed?

Scenario: Today your top college is emailing you about whether or not you were accepted. You have a few hours to wait until you'll get the email. When you think about waiting that long, you feel anxious.
Comprehension Question: Are you feeling relaxed while you wait to hear back from your top college?

Scenario: During gym class, you get tired faster than usual. Looking around, you notice that others seem full of energy. You think your classmates will assume you’re out of shape and you feel a flash of insecurity.
Scenario Body 2 (Resilience Only): You consider that strength and fitness can vary based on a number of factors, and you feel forgiving towards your body.
Comprehension Question: Do you come to feel forgiving toward your body once you consider that fitness can vary for many reasons?

Scenario: You finally get your driver’s license and ask your dad to borrow the family car to drive to the movies. As your dad hands you the keys, he looks tense and nervous. As you walk to the car, you think that his reaction to you driving alone for the first time is untrusting.
Scenario Body 2 (Resilience Only): You consider that he might just be nervous because there are many poor drivers on the roads, and you feel grateful that he cares.
Comprehension Question: Even after considering that many drivers are unpredictable, do you still believe your dad doesn't trust you?

Scenario: Someone in your grade posts a picture of the car their parents got them for their 16th birthday. Your family shares a single car, and your parents would not be able to afford to buy another one. You think about the gifts your parents have given you over the years, and you feel discouraged.
Scenario Body 2 (Resilience Only): Then you reflect on how your birthday celebrations with family have been filled with laughter, and feel better when you remember that gifts aren't the only way to feel valued.
Comprehension Question: Do you feel better remembering that gifts aren't the only way your family shows you're valued?

Scenario: You've been waiting to take your driving test for weeks, and you feel a thrill of excitment when you pass. You send a photo, but no one responds. You think your friends must find the photo annoying.
Scenario Body 2 (Resilience Only): After a few moments, you consider that they might not have seen the text yet, and your excitement returns.
Comprehension Question: Does considering that your friends may not have seen your text yet help your excitement return?

Scenario: You’re opening a debit account at the bank. As you chat with the bank teller, they use terms you barely understand. You wonder if the bank teller thinks you are childish.
Scenario Body 2 (Resilience Only): You consider that everyone has to start somewhere financially, and you feel confident in your ability to learn.
Comprehension Question: Does the bank teller actually think you're childish for not knowing certain financial terms?

Scenario: At the eye doctor, you’re told you need glasses for the first time. You imagine people at school saying you look weird. The thought makes you feel self-conscious.
Scenario Body 2 (Resilience Only): You remember that lots of classmates wear glasses without anyone caring much, and you feel excited to have a new accessory.
Comprehension Question: Do you end up feeling excited about your new glasses as a stylish accessory?

Scenario: You and your friends are looking through pictures from the recent school dance. You’re shorter and smaller than almost everyone at the school dance. You assume people think you look awkward.
Scenario Body 2 (Resilience Only): You consider that other people are focused on themselves, not you, and you feel better.
Comprehension Question: Are your classmates truly judging you for being shorter than everyone else at the dance?

Scenario: You’re hosting your Sweet Sixteen, a party you've been planning for months. A few of your friends text at the last minute that they can't make it. You think their response means they upset with you.
Scenario Body 2 (Resilience Only): You consider that plans can sometimes change last minute and teenagers don't always have control over their time, and you feel forgiving.
Comprehension Question: Do you feel forgiving toward your friends once you consider that plans can change unexpectedly?

Scenario: You’re getting ready for the school dance and your friends are all texting in the group chat. You notice your outfit suddenly looks way more casual than what your friends say they’re wearing. You suddenly worry your outfit is inappropriate.
Scenario Body 2 (Resilience Only): After a few minutes, you consider that your outfit makes you feel comfortable and happy, and you come away feeling satisfied with your choice.
Comprehension Question: Do you feel satisfied with your outfit once you focus on what makes you comfortable?

Scenario: You're getting ready before school picture day. As you're looking in the mirror, you notice a breakout on your forehead. You feel embarrassed about having acne in your yearbook photo.
Scenario Body 2 (Resilience Only): You consider that most people your age are dealing with their own skin issues, and you feel sympathetic towards yourself.
Comprehension Question: Are you the only person your age dealing with skin issues like acne?

Scenario: You are stocking shelves during your first shift at your new job. The manager stops by and lingers behind you for longer than expected. You think this means the manager finds you incompotent.
Scenario Body 2 (Resilience Only): You consider that a manager will often monitor new people to be helpful to them.
Comprehension Question: Do you consider that your manager might be lingering nearby simply to help you as a new employee?

Scenario: You’re practicing parallel parking for your driver’s test. As you drive around the parking lot with your parent, two kids from school walk by and glance over. You assume they’re judging your terrible parking and you feel embarrassed.
Scenario Body 2 (Resilience Only): You realize you can’t know what they thought, and you begin to feel relaxed.
Comprehension Question: Can you actually know for certain what those classmates were thinking when they glanced over?

Scenario: Your friend is celebrating their anniversary with their significant other and texts you a cute picture. Seeing the picture makes you think about how you've never been in a real relationship before. You imagine yourself celebrating an anniversary with your own significant other one day, and you feel dejected.
Scenario Body 2 (Resilience Only): Then you remind yourself that many people don’t find their significant other at this age, and you feel hopeful thinking about who you might meet in the future.
Comprehension Question: Do you feel hopeful about your future relationships once you remember many people haven't found a partner yet either?

Scenario: You are looking through stories on Snapchat after school one day. Your friend’s daily posts show them constantly out with people, while you mostly stay home. You assume you’re socially behind, so you feel self-conscious.
Scenario Body 2 (Resilience Only): You consider that energy levels and comfort zones vary, and everyone's social circles look different.
Comprehension Question: Do you consider that everyone's comfort zone and social circle look different?

Scenario: Your whole class is doing a career day exercise. A teacher asks what career you’re aiming for, and your mind goes blank. Your teacher probably thinks you are lazy.
Scenario Body 2 (Resilience Only): You remind yourself not knowing yet is normal.
Comprehension Question: Does your teacher actually think you're lazy for not having a career picked out yet?

Scenario: Your counselor calls you in to discuss scheduling for next semester and talk about future plans. You haven't thought much about what you want to do after college and your heart hammers as you walk towards his office. When you tell your counselor you feel unsure, you think he will be judgemental.
Scenario Body 2 (Resilience Only): As you open the door to his office, the counselor smiles, and you remember that he only wants to help.
Comprehension Question: Do you feel reassured when your counselor smiles, remembering he just wants to help you?

Scenario: You and your friends are seniors and getting ready to graduate next year. During lunch, someone asks what you’re doing after graduation, and you stumble over your answer. Your worry that your friends think its weird that you are still deciding.
Scenario Body 2 (Resilience Only): Then you remind yourself that most people are figuring it out too, and you end up feeling better.
Comprehension Question: Are you the only senior who hasn't figured out their after-graduation plans?

Scenario: Your older sibling just won another award at school. You watch your parents clap as they walk to the stage to accept their prize. When you think about the difference between their accomplishments and yours, you feel disappointed.
Scenario Body 2 (Resilience Only): But then you remind yourself that you have your own strengths, and you’re satisfied with the progress you’re making.
Comprehension Question: Do you feel satisfied with your own progress once you remember you have your own strengths?

Scenario: During dinner with your family, you get compared to your sibling who always gets straight A’s. You feel a twinge of resentment, wondering if you’ll ever measure up. When you mentally compare yourself to your sibling, you feel insecure.
Scenario Body 2 (Resilience Only): You allow yourself to consider your unique strengths, and you feel confident.
Comprehension Question: Do you feel confident once you allow yourself to consider your own unique strengths?

Scenario: Your parents want you to go to a specific college. You would rather go to a different college, but your parents have made it clear they are not on board with the school choice. When you think about talking with your parents about your choice, you feel nervous.
Scenario Body 2 (Resilience Only): You carefully think through your talking points, and you feel confident in your argument.
Comprehension Question: After preparing your talking points, do you still feel too nervous to talk with your parents?

Scenario: Your feed is full of friends posting scholarships, awards, and acceptance letters. You feel like you're falling apart while everyone else is moving forward. Then you remind yourself that struggling now doesn't mean you'll always be behind, and you feel steadier.
Comprehension Question: You think your struggle to keep up with friends' achievements means you will...
Correct Answer: eventually catch up in your own time.

Scenario: You've decided to go to community college after high school. You don't know anyone who is going to community college, and all of your friends are going to 4-year colleges. When you think about your decision, you feel like it's right for you.
Comprehension Question: You decide that choosing community college was...
Correct Answer: the right choice for your own future.
Incorrect Answer: a sign you couldn't get into a real college.

Scenario: You see your class valedictorian giving a perfect speech. You feel a pang of regret that that's not you. You remind yourself that success takes many forms, and you feel your regret ease.
Comprehension Question: When you watch the valedictorian's speech, you tell yourself that success...
Correct Answer: can look different for different people.
Incorrect Answer: will always be out of your reach.

Scenario: You scroll through your feed and see everyone achieving things like getting into college and getting straight As in all their classes. You aren't planning to go to college next year, and you feel a pit of insecurity in your stomach. You wonder if you aren't as accomplished as your classmates. However, you also know that social media is a highlight reel that doesn't tell the whole story.
Comprehension Question: You remind yourself that the achievements you see online are...
Correct Answer: just a highlight reel, not the full picture.
Incorrect Answer: proof that everyone else is ahead of you.

Scenario: You didn't get any special recognition at the ceremony while your friends won multiple awards. You sink down into your seat, feeling invisible. As you see the smiling faces of your friends on stage, you feel proud of them.
Comprehension Question: As your friends celebrate on stage, you tell yourself you feel...
Correct Answer: proud of them, even without an award yourself.

Scenario: You are lying on the couch scrolling through social media. You see lots of posts about people achieving awards or internships. You feel a pinch of inadequacy, but remind yourself that your path doesn’t need to look like theirs, and you feel the pressure ease.
Comprehension Question: Your path in life probably...
Correct Answer: doesn't need to look like anyone else's.
Incorrect Answer: isn't measuring up compared to theirs.

Scenario: Today, you will receive an important call. You'll find out if you got the job you interviewed for. As you think about waiting for the call, your anxiety is tolerable.
Comprehension Question: While you wait for the job call, you tell yourself your nerves are...
Correct Answer: manageable, even if you're a little anxious.
Incorrect Answer: too much for you to handle.

Scenario: Today your top college is emailing you about whether or not you were accepted. You have a few hours to wait until you'll get the email. When you think about waiting that long, you feel excited.
Comprehension Question: As the hours pass before the college email, you feel...
Correct Answer: excited to finally know the news.
Incorrect Answer: sick with dread about the answer.

Scenario: You hear your friends bragging about their dream colleges. You worry your choices seem “less impressive” and feel your stomach sink. You think your friends probably support your choice of colleges.
Comprehension Question: Your friends probably see your college choice as...
Correct Answer: just as worthwhile as their own choices.
Incorrect Answer: less impressive than where they're going.

Scenario: You notice your appetite has increased a lot lately. You worry people will think you eat too much. You remind yourself that your body needs the fuel to grow.
Comprehension Question: You remind yourself that your bigger appetite means...
Correct Answer: your body needs more fuel to grow right now.
Incorrect Answer: people will think you eat too much.

Scenario: Seeing news about canceled outdoor events due to weather, you start imagining missing big milestones in your own life. You worry climate change will take away opportunities before you reach them. You remind yourself that plans adapt and new opportunities can appear, so you begin to feel hopeful.
Comprehension Question: When you think about missing out on future milestones, you remind yourself that...
Correct Answer: plans can change and new chances can appear.
Incorrect Answer: opportunities could disappear before you get there.

Scenario: Your sibling's friend group seems huge while yours feels small. You start to think something’s wrong with you. You remind yourself that connection is about quality, not size, and you feel satisfied.
Comprehension Question: You decide that having a smaller friend group than your sibling means...
Correct Answer: you value quality connections over a big crowd.

Scenario: Your sibling picks up driving quickly while you’re still nervous behind the wheel. You worry you’re falling behind. You remind yourself that comfort will come with time, and you feel better.
Comprehension Question: The next time your sibling drives more smoothly than you, you will remind yourself that...
Correct Answer: comfort behind the wheel will come with practice.
Incorrect Answer: you're permanently worse at driving than they are.

Scenario: Your sibling gets their driver’s license before you. You feel embarrassed every time they offer you a ride. You remind yourself that you'll eventually get yours too, and you feel better.
Comprehension Question: Every time your sibling offers you a ride, you remind yourself that...
Correct Answer: you'll have your own license before long.
Incorrect Answer: you should feel embarrassed about needing rides.

Scenario: Your sibling already moved out and seems completely independent. You start to feel like you’ll never catch up. You remind yourself that independence happens in stages, and you feel content.
Comprehension Question: You decide that your sibling moving out means...
Correct Answer: independence happens in its own stages.
Incorrect Answer: you'll never catch up to where they are.

Scenario: Your classmates talk about saving money from their jobs. You still get an allowance. You remind yourself that independence looks different for everyone, and you feel lighter.
Comprehension Question: You remind yourself that still getting an allowance means...
Incorrect Answer: you're behind where you should already be.

Scenario: Your best friend already drives herself to school every day. You still get rides from your parents. You remind yourself that everyone's life progresses differently, and you feel greatful that your parents drive you.
Comprehension Question: You decide that still getting rides from your parents is...
Correct Answer: something you can feel grateful for right now.
Incorrect Answer: proof that you're less independent than your friend.

Scenario: You realize your best friend already knows how to budget and manage money. You still rely on your parents for help with your earnings. You remind yourself that independence comes in stages, and you feel patient with yourself.
Comprehension Question: You remind yourself that needing help managing your money means...
Correct Answer: independence comes in stages, and that's okay.
Incorrect Answer: you're behind your friend in growing up.

Scenario: You are scrolling on social media when you spot a post by one of your parents. As you read through, you see they are proudly postig about your sibling’s accomplishments online. Reading the post, you feel proud of your sibling.
Comprehension Question: When you read your parent's post about your sibling, you feel...

Scenario: Your mom pauses when you tell her what you want to do after graduation. You immediately think she disapproves. She might just be processing the idea, and you start to feel centered.
Comprehension Question: You decide your mom's pause after your news means she is...
Correct Answer: just taking a moment to process the idea.

Scenario: You notice your fellow classmates taking on more leadership roles in your school, but you haven't done anything like that yet. You worry you are falling behind. You then remember that everyone has their own path, and you feel reassured.
Comprehension Question: You remind yourself that not having a leadership role yet means...
Correct Answer: everyone follows their own path and timing.
Incorrect Answer: you're already falling behind your classmates.

Scenario: You are taking your SATs tomorrow. You know that the score you need to get into the college of your dreams is high. As you think about the test, you know that you are ready.
Comprehension Question: As you think about tomorrow's SAT, you tell yourself you are...
Correct Answer: ready, thanks to the work you've put in.
Incorrect Answer: certain to fail no matter what.

Scenario: People in class talk about their SAT practice scores, and yours feel lower. You assume you’re already falling behind so you feel discouraged. You remember these tests are designed to be learned gradualy.
Comprehension Question: You remind yourself that a lower practice score means...
Correct Answer: these skills are learned gradually with practice.
Incorrect Answer: you're already failing before the real test.

Scenario: You see photos from the varsity trip on social media. You wish you were there too. You remind yourself that everyone starts somewhere, and you feel calm turning your phone off.
Comprehension Question: You remind yourself that not being on the varsity trip yet means...
Correct Answer: everyone starts somewhere and works their way up.
Incorrect Answer: you don't really belong on the team.

Scenario: Your sibling gets into their first-choice college. You feel a sting of jealousy while congratulating them. You remind yourself that your path is still forming, and you feel grounded.
Comprehension Question: You remind yourself that your sibling's college acceptance means...
Correct Answer: your own path is still forming in its own time.
Incorrect Answer: you're already falling behind where you should be.

Scenario: Your family ends up traveling the same weekend as prom, and you can’t change it. You assume you’ll be the only one without prom photos to look back, and you feel a pang of sadness. When you think about your other good memories from high school, you feel grateful.
Comprehension Question: When you think about missing prom, you remind yourself that...
Correct Answer: you have plenty of other good memories from high school.
Incorrect Answer: you'll be the only one without special photos to look back on.

Scenario: You finally get your driver’s license and ask your dad to borrow the family car to drive to the movies. As your dad hands you the keys, he looks tense and nervous. As you walk to the car, you think that his reaction to you driving alone for the first time is understandable.
Comprehension Question: You decide your dad's nervous look while handing you the keys is...
Correct Answer: understandable, since it's your first time driving alone.
Incorrect Answer: a sign that he doesn't trust you.

Scenario: You’re practicing your signature for your first debit card, and it looks messy every time. You feel embarassed, worrying that the bank manager will see you as childish. As you drive to the bank, it occurs to you that the bank manager probably won't notice.
Comprehension Question: You think the bank manager will see your messy signature as...
Correct Answer: something they probably won't even notice.
Incorrect Answer: a reason to think you're childish.

Scenario: You start your first part-time job and make a small mistake on your first shift. Your manager sighs and looks annoyed but tells you that it's okay. They probably think you are learning.
Comprehension Question: You think your manager's sigh after your mistake means they...
Correct Answer: see it as a normal part of learning the job.
Incorrect Answer: think you're incompetent at your job.

Scenario: Your relationship ends, and you feel heartbreak like you never have before. You worry you’ll never feel okay again. You remind yourself that healing happens slowly, and you feel peaceful.
Comprehension Question: Will you ever feel okay again after this breakup?

Scenario: Your feed is full of couples posting anniversary posts and cute “how we met” stories. You start to feel behind, like you’re missing something important. Then you remind yourself that connection can happen at any point in life, and you feel hopeful.
Comprehension Question: Do you feel hopeful once you remind yourself that connection can happen at any point in life?

Scenario: Your classmates are planning for prom dates and talking about outfits. You don’t have a date yet. The thought of going alone makes you feel enthusiastic.
Comprehension Question: Does going to prom without a date make you feel dread?

Scenario: You’re the only one in your friend group who hasn’t had your first kiss. When your friends talk about their experiences, you feel embarrassed and left out. You remind yourself that real connection matters more than timing, and you feel compassion for yourself.
Comprehension Question: Do you feel compassion for yourself once you remind yourself connection matters more than timing?

Scenario: You had your first kiss before a lot of your friends, and you start to worry that people think you're too promiscuous. You then think back on the moment and how you enjoyed it, and you feel happy.
Comprehension Question: Do you end up feeling happy once you think back on enjoying that moment?

Scenario: You and your friends are going shopping for outfits for the upcoming school dance. You don't have a date to the dance yet, and you start to wonder what will happen if no one asks you. Shopping with your friends will probably be fun.
Comprehension Question: Are you worried that shopping with your friends won't be enjoyable without a date?

Scenario: You and your date are having a really fun time at the homecoming dance. Your prom date steps away to talk to someone from their math class for a few minutes and you feel a flash of anxiety - what if you are boring them? Your think that your date is most likley being friendly.
Comprehension Question: Do you think your date stepping away is most likely just them being friendly?

Scenario: At lunch, your friends compare stories about their relationships, laughing loudly over inside jokes. You notice yourself wondering whether your own relationship measures up somehow. You consider that every connection looks different from the outside, and you feel confident in your relationship.
Comprehension Question: Have you started doubting whether your relationship measures up after hearing your friends' stories?

Scenario: At lunch, your friends are talking about their dates for the school dance and what they are planning to wear. You feel sad that you don't have a date to the dance yet. If you go to the dance without a date, you will have a good time no matter what.
Comprehension Question: Do you believe you'll have a good time at the dance no matter what?

Scenario: Your friend is celebrating their anniversary with their significant other and texts you a cute picture. Seeing the picture makes you think about how you've never been in a real relationship before. You imagine yourself celebrating an anniversary with your own significant other one day, and you feel hopeful.
Comprehension Question: Do you feel hopeful imagining your own future anniversary one day?

Scenario: You see someone’s feed full of travel and perfect outfits. You compare it to your own feed and feel like you’re falling behind. Then you remember that people only post highlights, not real life, and you feel balanced.
Comprehension Question: Are you actually falling behind compared to the people you see online?

Scenario: You scroll through posts about people achieving awards or internships. You feel like you’re falling behind. Then you remind yourself that your path doesn’t need to look like theirs, and you feel the sense of pressure ease.
Comprehension Question: Does the sense of pressure ease once you remind yourself your path doesn't need to match theirs?

Scenario: It's the fall of your senior year, and you play for a school sports team. You scroll through social media and see teammates posting commitment announcements and feel a lump in your throat, wondering if that will ever be you. You remind yourself that recruiting happens on different timelines, and you feel calmer.
Comprehension Question: Does seeing teammates post commitments mean your own recruiting timeline has failed?

Scenario: Your mom tells you to call the pizza place to order dinner for your family. Talking on the phone makes you super anxious, and you feel your heart start to race and your breathing speed up as you pick up the phone. You remind yourself that the person at the pizza place will probably not even remember you in five minutes, and you feel better.
Comprehension Question: Do you feel better once you remind yourself the pizza worker likely won't remember the call?

Scenario: Your friend is giving a presentation in English class and she seems totally confident and calm. During your presentation, your hands shook and your stomach felt twisted with nerves. When you think about how public speaking doesn't come as naturally to you, you feel compassion for yourself.
Comprehension Question: Do you feel compassion for yourself once you accept that public speaking doesn't come naturally to everyone?

Scenario: The friend who agreed to go with you tells you they’re sick the day before prom. You assume everyone will think you got ditched. You remind yourself that lots of other friends will be there, and you feel happy about going.
Comprehension Question: Will everyone at prom think you got ditched by your friend?

Scenario: You’re filling out an online application for a weekend job, and one question asks for “relevant experience.” You don't have many work experiences, and feel uncomfortable looking at your limited resume. The employers will probably think this is appropriate.
Comprehension Question: Do you think employers will probably see your application as appropriate?

Scenario: You get home from your job and see your friends posting about hanging out. You feel a flash of FOMO and wonder if you’re missing your “teen years.” Then you think about how everyone finds their own balance, and you feel content remembering you find time for what matters.
Comprehension Question: Are you actually missing out on your teen years by having a job?

Scenario: Most of your friends already have a job lined up for summer vacation. It's almost the end of the school year and you haven't even started applying. You think about the different types of jobs you could apply for, and you feel motivated.
Comprehension Question: Do you feel motivated once you start thinking about the types of jobs you could apply for?

Scenario: You see someone your age has gone viral for something cool. You feel like you’re not doing anything meaningful. Then you remind yourself that going viral isn’t the same as being fulfilled, and you feel centered.
Comprehension Question: Do you feel centered once you remind yourself that going viral isn't the same as being fulfilled?

Scenario: Your voice sounds different and more high-pitched than your friends'. You cringe, wondering if people think you sound childish. You remember that growing up isn’t a race, and you feel satisfied with your body.
Comprehension Question: Would people really think your voice sounds childish?

Scenario: Your classmates all seem to know what kind of people they want to be after high school. You still feel unsure of who you are. You remind yourself that figuring yourself out takes time, and you know things will turn out as they should.
Comprehension Question: Do you trust that things will turn out as they should once you remind yourself figuring yourself out takes time?

Scenario: You say goodbye to your classmates after senior year. You feel anxious about losing touch. You remind yourself that endings can also start new chapters, and you feel bittersweet.
Comprehension Question: Does losing touch with classmates mean those friendships are erased forever?

Scenario: Your counselor calls you in to discuss scheduling for next semester and talk about future plans. You haven't thought much about what you want to do after college and your heart hammers as you walk towards his office. When you tell your counselor you feel unsure, you think he will be understanding.
Comprehension Question: Do you believe your counselor will be understanding about your uncertainty?

Scenario: You and your friends are seniors and getting ready to graduate next year. During lunch, someone asks what you’re doing after graduation, and you stumble over your answer. Your friends probably think its okay that you are still deciding.
Comprehension Question: Do you believe your friends probably think it's okay that you're still deciding?

Scenario: You'e looking forward to applying for jobs, but you are having trouble writing your first resumè. As you stare at the blank page, you worry that you don't have enough experiene to qualify for the jobs you want. You think your application will probably be appropriate.
Comprehension Question: Are you truly lacking enough experience to qualify for the jobs you want?

Scenario: Your friend talks nonstop about internships, and you can’t relate. You start to worry you’re unambitious. Then you remember your goals just look different, and you start to feel confident.
Comprehension Question: Do you feel confident once you remember your goals simply look different from your friend's?

Scenario: A group of your friends are talking about getting allowance from their parents. Your parents can't afford to give you an allowence, and you have to work a job after school to make money. Your friends proabbly think you are hard-working.
Comprehension Question: Would your friends look down on you for having to work after school?

Scenario: Your friends are posting about college visits, and you feel like you're missing out because you're not following the same route. You think they might judge your choice. Then you remember that many people find success without a four-year degree, and you feel happier about your decision.
Comprehension Question: Do you feel happier about your decision once you remember many people succeed without a four-year degree?

Scenario: A teacher asks what career you’re aiming for, and your mind goes blank. You feel small and embarrassed. You remind yourself not knowing yet is normal.
Comprehension Question: Do you remind yourself that not knowing your future career yet is completely normal?

Scenario: Someone asks about your college plans, and you hesitate before saying you’re not going. You brace for judgment. Then they just nod and talk about gap years, and you begin to feel oddly relieved.
Comprehension Question: Does everyone judge you harshly for not having college plans yet?

Scenario: Your friend posts that they got the internship you applied for too. You feel jealous and start thinking you're not good enough. Then you remind yourself that one opportunity doesn’t define your path, and you start to feel hopeful.
